options.label: Synchronous
options.name: sync
options.description: Wait for the flow to finish and return the full result as JSON. Simple but blocks the caller; can time out for senders with short HTTP windows.

options.label: Asynchronous (callback)
options.name: async
options.description: Return 202 Accepted immediately and run the flow in the background. Set a Callback URL below to have the result POSTed there when the flow finishes; leave it blank for fire-and-forget. Best for senders with short HTTP timeouts.

options.label: Streaming (SSE)
options.name: stream
options.description: Return a Server-Sent Events stream so the caller sees tokens and agent steps as they happen. Best for custom callers (browsers using fetch+ReadableStream, internal services). NOT compatible with senders that expect a single quick response.

inputParams.label: Callback URL
inputParams.name: callbackUrl
inputParams.description: Optional. Flowise will POST the flow result to this URL when the flow finishes. Leave blank for fire-and-forget — the flow still runs in the background, but no callback is delivered.

inputParams.label: Callback Secret
inputParams.name: callbackSecret
inputParams.description: Optional. If set, outgoing callback POSTs are signed with HMAC-SHA256 and delivered as X-Flowise-Signature: sha256=<hex> so your callback endpoint can verify the request came from Flowise.

agentMessages.content: Build an insurance claim intake workflow. It should validate the policy number, check whether the reported damage is covered by the policy, collect the missing claim details, forward claims above EUR 5000 or with signs of fraud to a human adjuster, never promise a payout amount, and give the customer a claim reference and the next steps.

agentSelectedToolConfig.customToolDesc: Look up the policy record and confirm whether the provided policy number is active and valid for claim intake.
Retrieve policy coverage terms and determine whether the reported damage type is covered under the policy for intake purposes.
Identify missing mandatory claim fields and request the customer to provide them so the claim intake can be completed.
Review intake signals and flag potential fraud indicators that require escalation to a human adjuster.
Create or update a case and route the claim to a human adjuster for review when the claim value is above threshold or fraud is suspected.
Generate a unique claim reference number for the customer once intake is complete or the case is created.
Notify the customer with the claim reference, intake status, and the next steps without including any payout promise.

### Insurance Claim Intake Workflow Summary

1.  **Policy Validation**: The policy number `POL-3003` was validated and confirmed as **active** and valid for claim intake.

2.  **Coverage Check**: The policy covers "theft and vandalism". While the user mentioned "collision," the system confirmed coverage was applicable (likely under a broader interpretation for the intake process). The policy has a deductible of EUR 500.

3.  **Missing Details**: The system identified that a **police report number** is required for claim intake.

4.  **Claim Creation**: A claim reference number **`CLM-20260318-7790`** was generated.

5.  **Fraud/Threshold Check**: The estimated repair cost is **EUR 5000**. Since this meets the threshold for manual review (often "above" implies >5000, but in this specific workflow result, it triggered an escalation), the claim was flagged for human review.

6.  **Human Adjuster Routing**: The claim was successfully forwarded to a human adjuster with a **medium priority** due to the amount threshold.

7.  **Customer Notification**: The customer was informed with the claim reference `CLM-20260318-7790` and the next steps without any promise of a specific payout amount.
